decors.name: Carceri
decors.author: Giovanni Battista Piranesi (c.1750)
decors.summary: A Piranesi imaginary prison vaulting into bone shadow.
decors.description: The Drawbridge, a plate from Piranesi's Carceri d'Invenzione (c.1750) - impossible stairs, bridges, and engines of stone - dithered into stark Ryoku bone.

decors.name: Melencolia I
decors.author: Albrecht Dürer (1514)
decors.summary: Dürer's brooding angel of genius, drawn in bone stipple.
decors.description: Albrecht Dürer's 1514 master engraving Melencolia I - the winged figure, the magic square, and the scattered instruments of thought - reduced to Ryoku's one-bit bone line.

decors.name: Deer in Motion
decors.author: Eadweard Muybridge (1887)
decors.summary: Muybridge's deer, caught mid-stride across the frame.
decors.description: A plate from Eadweard Muybridge's Animal Locomotion (1887) - fallow deer stepping through a wooded run, frame by frame - baked to Ryoku bone.

decors.name: Pillars of Creation
decors.author: NASA, ESA / STScI (Hubble)
decors.summary: The Eagle Nebula's Pillars of Creation in bone light.
decors.description: The Hubble Space Telescope's Pillars of Creation - towers of interstellar gas and dust in the Eagle Nebula - dithered so the starlight reads as Ryoku bone.

decors.name: Red Fuji
decors.author: Katsushika Hokusai (c.1830)
decors.summary: Hokusai's Red Fuji under a streaked morning sky.
decors.description: Fine Wind, Clear Morning (Red Fuji) from Hokusai's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji - the bare peak and its cloud-banded sky - reduced to Ryoku's one-bit bone.

decors.name: The Rhinoceros
decors.author: Albrecht Dürer (1515)
decors.summary: Dürer's armoured rhinoceros woodcut, one-bit and bone.
decors.description: The Rhinoceros (1515), Dürer's famous woodcut of a beast he never saw, plated in riveted armour - baked to bone-on-transparent stipple.

decors.name: Trebonianus Gallus
decors.author: Roman bronze, The Met (Open Access, CC0)
decors.summary: A bronze Roman emperor, arm raised, cast in bone.
decors.description: The Metropolitan Museum's over-life-size bronze of the emperor Trebonianus Gallus (251-253 CE), his silhouette reduced to Ryoku's one-bit bone.
